title: ACH Retry Test Plan
brief: Produce a concise validation checklist for the ACH retry change before it enters user acceptance testing.

delegate.scenario: The payment-platform team has added retry handling for failed ACH transfers, and the release candidate is ready for validation. The QA lead and an on-call engineer will use the checklist during testing next week to decide whether the change is ready for user acceptance testing.
delegate.inputs:
ACH retry change, release candidate 3.8.2. QA runs in the staging environment; use synthetic accounts only. A retry is allowed once after a network timeout, but not after an account-closed response. Confirm the ledger records only one debit, even if the gateway times out after accepting the request.

Coverage requested:
- Timeout and successful retry: 18 cases
- Account closed; no retry: 16 cases
- Duplicate request and ledger behavior: 12 cases
Planned total: 48 cases

Use the existing ACH sandbox and capture request IDs, gateway responses, and ledger entries. Do not include real account or routing numbers in screenshots. The QA lead owns execution; the payments engineer reviews failures. Stop testing and notify the release manager if a duplicate debit is observed. UAT sign-off is scheduled for 04/21/2026. The release calendar lists ACH retry UAT sign-off as 04/22/2026. Record each case as pass, fail, or blocked, with a short evidence link. The team needs the checklist by 04/17/2026.
delegate.goal: A good result lets QA execute the change safely, record consistent evidence, and escalate failures before UAT.

criteria.text: Says the checklist is for the QA lead and payments engineer validating the release candidate.
Uses the stated staging environment and synthetic-account constraint.
Provides an executable checklist with a clear, concise format and length.
Asks the AI to verify coverage totals against the listed test categories.
Asks the AI to check requirements, expected outcomes, and escalation steps for consistency.
Includes privacy-safe evidence handling and a check for duplicate financial effects.

traps.description: The listed category counts add up to 46, but the stated planned total is 48.
evidence: Duplicate request and ledger behavior: 12 cases

traps.description: The UAT sign-off is assigned two different dates.

delegate.exemplar: Create a concise, numbered validation checklist for the QA lead and payments engineer to use on release candidate 3.8.2 in staging. Use synthetic accounts and the ACH sandbox, and include clear steps, expected results, evidence to capture, and stop/escalation conditions. Check that the requirements and test coverage are internally consistent, including the category counts and dates; list any conflicts or assumptions for the team to resolve rather than choosing a value. Include privacy-safe evidence guidance and verify the duplicate-debit safeguard. Keep the checklist practical to execute before UAT.
